title: CHUCOLATE: Current Knowledge and Prevalence of LATE-NC in Geriatric Memory Clinics at a Memory Center in Lorraine
official: CHUCOLATE: Current Knowledge and Prevalence of LATE-NC in Geriatric Memory Clinics at a Memory Center in Lorraine
summary:
LATE syndrome (Limbic-predominant Age-related TDP-43 Encephalopathy) is a neurocognitive disorder associated with TDP-43 proteinopathy, whose clinical presentation-a hippocampal amnestic syndrome-is similar to that of Alzheimer's disease. There are no specific markers to differentiate between the two, other than the exclusion of Alzheimer's biomarkers (AB), a criterion limited by the possibility of comorbidity. In the era of anti-amyloid therapies, it is crucial to differentiate between them in order to appropriately offer these therapies to patients. The clinical diagnosis of LATE is therefore of great importance. A pattern specific to LATE has been described on PET-CT and may facilitate this diagnosis.

To study the concordance between the PET-CT pattern and the clinical criteria for LATE, we will compare changes in MMSE scores over one year between patients classified as "LATE" or "AD" based on 18F-FDG PET-CT.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* \- An FDG-PET/CT scan at the Nancy University Hospital
* A neuropsychological evaluation within 6 months of the FDG-PET/CT scan
* A neuropsychological follow-up 1 year after the initial evaluation

Exclusion Criteria:

* Lack of follow-up at the Nancy University Hospital (CHRU) or at the Nancy Geriatric Research and Treatment Center (CMRR) for all of these criteria
* Not enrolled in a social security program
* Presence of another neurological, neurodevelopmental, or psychiatric condition that could explain the cognitive impairments
* Refusal to allow the use of the data
